title: Recollecting the teaching
hookLine: one teacher makes a hard thing click; another makes an easy thing impossible. what does 'well taught' mean?
tomorrow: who practices well, and why call them to mind?

cards: A good teacher can make a hard thing click in one afternoon. A muddled one can make an easy thing impossible. Same subject, different teaching.
Yesterday's question asked what makes a teaching well taught, and the old chant opens on exactly that word: svakkhato bhagavata dhammo. Well taught by the Blessed One is the dhamma.
Buddhaghosa stops on that first word and asks what it means.

teach.h: GOOD IN THE BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END.
teach.b: His answer borrows a phrase the suttas use again and again: good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, right in meaning and in wording. And he applies it at every size.
A single verse, good in its first line, its middle and its last.

teach.h: A VERSE, A SUTTA, THE WHOLE PATH.
teach.b: A whole sutta, from its setting to its close. The whole path: good conduct at the beginning, calm and insight in the middle, freedom at the end. Well taught means it holds together at every scale, with no filler.
Now a neighbor. In the Torah, Moses tells Israel the commandment isn't hidden or far off, and isn't up in heaven where someone must go and fetch it.
In the King James words: "But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it."

teach.h: A COMMANDMENT, OR A TEACHING FOUND.
teach.b: Here's what they share: a teaching meant to be close, spoken and lived, not admired from a distance. And one honest difference. Deuteronomy's word is a commandment from God, part of a covenant with a people.
The dhamma is described as something the Buddha found and taught, with no one commanding it, to be seen by each person for themselves. Different roots, the same nearness.
A teaching that's well taught doesn't stay on the page.

how: Theravada Buddhists chant the recollection of the dhamma, svakkhato bhagavata dhammo, in daily and temple chanting; as a meditation its qualities are called to mind one at a time, as Visuddhimagga 7 describes.

o: studying a monastery's rules before ordination day
memorizing the Buddha's sermons word for word in Pali
calling to mind the dhamma's qualities, starting with well taught

games.q: well taught, at every size — tap the pairs.

s: svakkhato means the dhamma is old, and so it must be true
it means well taught: good in the beginning, the middle and the end.
Deuteronomy says the commandment isn't in heaven but very near, in the mouth and the heart
a neighbor's way of saying a teaching is meant to be lived.
Deuteronomy and the dhamma verse agree on who gives the teaching
Deuteronomy's word is a commandment from God; the dhamma is described as found and taught by the Buddha, seen by each for themselves.

games.q: your cousin's coach writes one sentence on the whiteboard each week, and the team actually uses it. by today's lesson, what makes it well taught?
o: it's short, so it's easy for everyone to memorize.
it holds together, and it's close enough to use in a game.
it comes from someone with the right title and rank.
games.why: well taught means good from beginning to end, and near enough to live: in thy mouth and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write svakkhato, well taught, slowly. Under it, write one thing someone once taught you well: a coach, a grandparent, a friend. Look at the two lines together and notice what made the second one stick.

wordCard.voice: Recollecting the teaching: calling the dhamma's qualities to mind, starting with svakkhato, well taught.

orig.note: Pali: well taught, well proclaimed. The first quality in the recollection of the dhamma.

carryVoice: Keep this one: well taught, good in the beginning, the middle and the end. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 7 (recollection of the dhamma: 'well proclaimed' because good in the beginning, the middle and the end, applied to a stanza, a sutta and the whole dispensation, virtue as the beginning, serenity and insight the middle, fruition and nibbana the end)

Recollection of the dhamma (svakkhato bhagavata dhammo …), as in SN 11.3; the stock phrase 'good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing', as in DN 2

sources.q: But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it.

sources.ref: Deuteronomy 30:11-13 (the commandment is not hidden, not far off, not in heaven, not beyond the sea)
